name: Ebussu'ud Efendi
bio: Ebussu'ud Efendi (1490-1574) was born near Constantinople into a family of Kurdish origin. After a career in judicial posts he became Seyhulislam, the chief mufti of the Ottoman Empire, under Suleyman the Magnificent and Selim II, and held the office for some thirty years until his death.

He is remembered above all as a jurist, whose fetvas and legal treatises shaped Ottoman law. He also wrote verse, chiefly in Arabic and Turkish; E. J. W. Gibb, in his History of Ottoman Poetry, preserves a Turkish elegy on a beloved child, translated below.

poems.title: Come, O thou blessed of spright, my angel of light, O come!
poems.author: Ebussu'ud Efendi
poems.collection: A History of Ottoman Poetry, vol. III (1904)
poems.text:
Come, O thou blessed of spright, my angel of light, O come!
Forspent for my yearning sore are my strength and my might, O come!

Methought when I laid thee to rest that my life would vanish away;
But alack! it is come not to pass, that fancy unright; O come!

With thee was the realm of my life with fairest estate beseen;
But now is it all o'erthrown, and dreary my plight; O come!

O thou, who makest thy tears to rain as a cloud! as to Fate,
Me too hath it made to weep; let our tears unite, O come!

Of prayer and entreaty at length thou hast made an end, O heart,
That dear comes not, so to him let us fare forthright, O come!
